name: Nás
sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The Fir Bolg reached Ireland under their leader Dela, the people the extract calls NASA. Dela split the island among his sons. Gann and Sengann took Munster. Leinster went to Slane, and Ulster to Rudraige. Notable Fir Bolg kings included Eochaid mac Eirc, master of the central province with his wife Tailtiu. Rinnal devised spear points. Delga raised Dun Delgan, the fort later called Dundalk in Co. Louth. The Fir Bolg also counted the healer Fingein Fisiochda and the hero Sreng among them. The Fir Bolg held power for just 37 years before the Tuatha De Danann appeared. At the first fight at Mag Tuired, Nuada pushed the Fir Bolg from Ireland at the cost of his arm and his throne. The defeated Fir Bolg fell back to the Aran Islands, where their king Aonghus built Dun Aongusa, and to islands off Scotland and wild Connemara. Their memory survives in place-names such as Dun Bolg (Co. Wicklow), Moherbullog (Co. Clare), and Moyboulogue (Co. Cavan).

okr.objective: Nas is the name behind the account of the Fir Bolg and their rule of Ireland.
key_results: Dela divided Ireland among his sons, giving each province a ruler.
Notable Fir Bolg kings included Eochaid mac Eirc, Rinnal, and Delga.
The Fir Bolg ruled 37 years before the Tuatha De Danann arrived.
Nuada drove them out at Mag Tuired, losing his arm and his throne in the process.
